recognize_zh: 血片中的淋巴球核分成多葉、呈花瓣狀（flower cell），是成人 T 細胞白血病/淋巴瘤（ATLL）的特徵；右側手部 X 光可見中節指骨兩側骨膜下骨吸收（箭頭處），反映 ATLL 相關的高血鈣與骨吸收。
features: Medium-sized lymphoid cells with deeply lobulated, clover-leaf ('flower cell') nuclei
Hand radiograph with subperiosteal bone resorption along the radial and ulnar margins of the middle phalanges (arrowheads)
Second radiograph shows smoother cortical outlines of the phalanges compared with the first
describe_en: Composite figure. Peripheral blood smears (A, B) show atypical lymphoid cells with markedly convoluted, multilobated 'flower-like' nuclei, condensed chromatin, and scant basophilic cytoplasm. A plain radiograph of the hand (C) demonstrates subperiosteal bone resorption along the cortical margins of multiple phalanges (arrowheads), a pattern resembling hyperparathyroid bone disease; a second radiograph (D) shows less conspicuous cortical irregularity, presumably after treatment. Findings are consistent with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma with skeletal involvement related to increased osteoclastic bone resorption and hypercalcemia.

ddx.vs: Sezary cells have cerebriform, finely grooved nuclei rather than petal-like lobation, and are HTLV-1 negative.
T-PLL cells have a visible nucleolus and cytoplasmic blebs, with TCL1 rearrangement, and lack flower-shaped nuclei and HTLV-1 integration.
Identical subperiosteal resorption on radiographs occurs in hyperparathyroidism, but PTH is elevated, whereas ATLL-related hypercalcemia is PTHrP-mediated with suppressed PTH.
Neutrophils have pink granular cytoplasm and thin chromatin bridges between discrete lobes rather than a single convoluted lymphoid nucleus.
